generated_note: Hand-curated from this project's own real validation status reports (naip/docs/STATUS_WEEK*.md), not a raw model-output export. Every number here was checked directly against the cited source document, not restated from memory. This page shows cross-year/cross-event generalization tests of models already trained against genuinely independent real ground truth from the start (FIRMS, IOM/NDMA, FAO, MNFSR) -- it is not a proxy-trained model being checked against real events for the first time.

events.title: Fire detector — 2021 replay
events.model_label: Track E/K thermal-only GBT fire classifier — unchanged, persisted checkpoint, no retraining
events.metric_detail: Precision 0.230 (vs. 0.245 on the original 2023 test), recall 0.763 (vs. 0.587), ROC-AUC 0.786 (vs. 0.737). The 2021 comparison uses the full 15-date grid vs. the original's narrower 3-date test split — a harder bar, not an easier one.
events.ground_truth_source: NASA FIRMS VIIRS active-fire hotspots, national bbox, 15 real dates, 50km/±1-day tolerance (83,066 real hotspot rows pulled for the window)
events.how_measured: The persisted 2023-trained model (never retrained) was replayed against a real, entirely unseen 2021 burning season — a genuinely different year, selected because it had the highest real FIRMS hotspot density of four candidate years checked (2020/2021/2022/2024). Labels came from the same real FIRMS cross-reference methodology used for the original 2023 dataset.
events.limits: Two real years is real, useful evidence of generalization, not permanent proof across every possible burning-season condition. Both years share the same national bbox and the same MSG sensor/product — a third year, or a genuinely different region, would still add real information.

events.title: Flood risk model — 2024 fair test
events.window: 2024 monsoon season — 14 real government-declared calamity districts (positive) + 112 real not-declared districts (negative), 126 total
events.model_label: Track I v3, precipitation-augmented GBT flood classifier — now the deployed live model (promoted Week 27)
events.metric_baseline_label: Original Track D model, same 2024 fair test
events.metric_detail: Precision 0.190, recall 0.862, AUC 0.761. The score-separation gap between flooded/not-flooded predictions is 0.332 — over 3x the original model's own 0.096 gap, and the opposite of the rejected v2 attempt's collapsed 0.012 gap on the same test.
events.ground_truth_source: IOM/Shelter Cluster government-declared calamity district list (16 Sept 2022 precedent methodology, applied to the real 2024 disaster year) cross-checked against real Sentinel-1 SAR + CHIRPS precipitation features
events.how_measured: This is the exact fair, labeled, full-2024 test that caught the rejected v2 attempt's failure (a real, independently verified negative result from Week 14) — same methodology reused to test v3's real precipitation-feature addition. v3's real permutation importance confirms precip_anomaly_pct is the single highest-importance feature (0.128), not noise: mean anomaly for flooded vs. not-flooded points is +216.4% vs. +94.6%, in the physically expected direction.
events.limits: Absolute precision (0.190) means most 'flooded' predictions on a genuinely new year are still wrong more often than right — this is real, meaningful improvement over the original (0.134) and the rejected v2 (0.107), not a solved problem. A live-replay run the same week found 9 flagged districts with real precipitation anomalies in the opposite direction from the training data's own correlation — a genuine, unresolved open question, not smoothed over.

events.title: Locust breeding-risk — 2020 backtest
events.window: Jan–May 2020 (real tail of the 2019–2021 upsurge), 49 real confirmed hopper/band events (stratified sample of 291 real event clusters)
events.model_label: locust_breeding_risk.py's real-time soil-moisture/NDVI logic, replayed with each event's own date substituted as "asof"
events.metric_baseline_label: Original thresholds (SM anomaly ≥0.02, NDVI delta ≥0.03), same 49 real events
events.metric_detail: 12/49 events caught after recalibration, vs. 3/49 before. SM-anomaly alone at ≥0.02 already caught 22/49 (44.9%) — the real bottleneck was the NDVI "green-up" framing, which doesn't fit these arid breeding regions (real median NDVI delta at confirmed events was -0.011, slight browning, not greening).
events.ground_truth_source: FAO Desert Locusts Observations dataset, hopper+band records only, Pakistan (country code PA)
events.how_measured: NDVI_GREENUP_DELTA was relaxed from 0.03 to -0.05 ("not markedly browning" instead of "greening") based directly on the real median delta found at confirmed events; SM_ANOMALY_FAVORABLE (0.02) was left unchanged.
events.limits: The FAO extract has real confirmed-presence events only — no real confirmed-absence records exist, so only recall could be validated here, never precision or a false-alarm rate. The recalibration is real and data-driven, but its cost in false positives is genuinely unknown. All 49 events come from a single real 2020 upsurge episode — do not over-generalize to all future locust behavior.

events.title: Crop-share model — cross-year validation
events.window: 2021-22 ↔ 2022-23, bidirectional (same 2,875 real Sentinel-2 points both directions)
events.ground_truth_source: MNFSR district-wise Crops Area & Production reports, 2021-22 and 2022-23 seasons, each independently parsed and cross-validated against its own printed provincial totals (5% tolerance)
events.how_measured: A genuine temporal holdout, not a spatial one — train on one real MNFSR-labeled year's crop shares, test on the other, both directions. Same no-lat/lon discipline and pre-headline permutation-importance check as every other model here; both directions confirm real phenology metrics (evi_annual_mean, ndwi_peak_value, evi_trough_value) drive the result, not a district-identity shortcut.
events.limits: Wheat/cotton/rice show real, expected degradation under this harder cross-year test, consistent in both directions. Sugarcane is a real, honest exception — both cross-year directions score positive R², a real improvement over the original's catastrophic -1.120 — but the most likely real explanation is that each cross-year direction trains on all 115 districts, vs. the original's thinner 81-district spatial split, not a validated fix for the rare-crop signal problem itself.

events.title: Yield prediction — cross-year validation (negative result)
events.model_label: Track O per-crop HistGradientBoostingRegressor, Sentinel-2 phenology features
events.ground_truth_source: MNFSR real reported yield (production ÷ area), independently cross-validated against printed provincial totals (5% tolerance), both 2021-22 and 2022-23 seasons
events.how_measured: A real, cheap, zero-model naive baseline ("this district's yield this year = its real reported yield the other real year") was compared against the trained Sentinel-2 phenology model, both directions, per crop.
events.limits: The naive baseline beats the trained model in 6 of 8 crop×direction combinations. The 2 cases the model "wins" (cotton both directions, rice direction B) are cases where both model and baseline score clearly negative R² — a "which is less bad" result, not a genuine win. Real district-level wheat yield is highly persistent year-over-year in this data (naive R²≈0.77-0.78) — a genuinely high bar satellite phenology from a different year has little room to clear. This is a real finding about the task's difficulty, not a modeling failure to fix by tuning harder. Reported here, not omitted, on purpose.
